epics.title: Real Document Upload API Integration
epics.jtbd: When a user uploads a document, I want the system to actually send the file to the backend and verify the response, so that the document is reliably stored and failures are transparent.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Upload success rate without silent failures
requirements: R1: The frontend must send the uploaded document to the real backend API.
R2: The frontend must wait for a verified response from the backend before showing a success message.
R3: If the upload fails or the backend is unreachable, the frontend must explicitly display an error instead of faking success.

slices.title: Frontend Document Upload Integration
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend upload for this epic, I want to replace the stub with a real network fetch, so that the document is sent to the backend.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the document upload form,
When a user selects a file and submits,
Then a real network request is made to the backend and the UI awaits the response, with WCAG 2.1 AA compliant loading indicators.

slices.title: QA Document Upload Integration
slices.jtbd: When verifying the upload flow for this epic, I want to test successful and failed network requests, so that the frontend handles real backend states correctly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the QA environment,
When the upload flow is tested with a real backend and a simulated network failure,
Then both the success and error states are verified end-to-end.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Test pass rate for error handling

epics.title: Data Subject Rights Management
epics.jtbd: When the product stores personal data, I want data subjects to be able to request export or erasure of their data within statutory deadlines, so that privacy compliance is maintained.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Compliance with GDPR request handling deadlines
epics.tocConstraintRef: Missing UI for existing backend privacy endpoints
requirements: R1: The UI must provide a privacy settings section for users to manage their data.
R2: The UI must allow users to trigger a data export request.
R3: The UI must allow users to trigger an account erasure request, calling the existing backend endpoints.

slices.title: Frontend Privacy Settings UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the privacy UI for this epic, I want to expose the export and erasure actions, so that users can exercise their statutory rights.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a logged-in user,
When they navigate to privacy settings,
Then they can initiate export and erasure requests with WCAG 2.1 AA compliant controls.

slices.title: QA Data Subject Rights UI
slices.jtbd: When testing the privacy UI for this epic, I want to verify the connection to the backend endpoints, so that the statutory features work end-to-end.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a user account with data,
When an erasure and export request are triggered via the UI,
Then the backend correctly processes the requests and the UI updates accordingly.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Pass rate for privacy integration tests

epics.title: Resolve Frontend Integration and Statutory Requirements
epics.jtbd: When the end customer accesses the application, I want a stable, self-contained frontend with a reachable imprint, so that the application loads reliably and complies with domain legal requirements.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Availability of the statutory Imprint page
requirements: R1: A dedicated page or modal containing the legally required Imprint (Impressum) information must be implemented.
R2: The footer link must correctly navigate to the Imprint page instead of a dead link.
R3: The imprint page must contain realistic domain content for a legal entity to demonstrate compliance on a fresh install.

slices.title: Frontend Imprint Page Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the imprint page for this epic, I want to create a dedicated view and wire the footer link, so that the legal requirement is met.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the application footer,
When the user clicks the Imprint link,
Then they are taken to a valid, WCAG 2.1 AA compliant Imprint page populated with realistic legal entity content.

slices.title: QA Imprint Navigation
slices.jtbd: When verifying the imprint for this epic, I want to ensure the link works and content is accessible, so that the compliance is proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the deployed application,
When testing navigation,
Then the imprint page loads successfully from the footer without any dead links.

epics.title: User Consent Management for Tracking
epics.jtbd: When the product collects telemetry data, I want an opt-in consent mechanism, so that privacy compliance is maintained before non-essential scripts load.
requirements: R1: A consent banner must be displayed to the user before loading any telemetry or tracking scripts.
R2: Telemetry collection and non-essential cookies must remain blocked until explicit opt-in consent is given.
R3: The user must be able to revoke consent as easily as they gave it.

slices.title: Frontend Consent Banner Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing consent for this epic, I want to block trackers by default and show a banner, so that opt-in rules are enforced.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new visitor,
When they load the application,
Then a WCAG 2.1 AA compliant consent banner is shown and no telemetry is sent until they opt-in.

slices.title: QA Consent Enforcement
slices.jtbd: When testing consent for this epic, I want to verify that telemetry is actually blocked, so that the application is legally compliant.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a clean browser state,
When loading the app without interacting with the banner,
Then no tracking network requests are fired.

epics.title: Strict Document Download Resource Identification
epics.jtbd: When a user requests a document download, I want the system to either return the exact stored document or return a 404 error, so that missing documents are correctly identified and not hallucinated.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Accurate 404 response rate for non-existent documents
requirements: R1: The download endpoint must verify the document's existence in the persistent repository.
R2: If the document is not found, the backend must return a 404 Not Found status instead of generating fallback content.

slices.title: Backend Document Validation
slices.jtbd: When fixing the download endpoint for this epic, I want to remove the orElseGet fallback, so that missing records throw an appropriate error.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the document API,
When requesting a non-existent document ID,
Then the server returns a strict 404 Not Found response without generating content.

slices.title: QA Document Validation
slices.jtbd: When testing the download endpoint for this epic, I want to assert the 404 response, so that we guarantee no hallucinated content is served.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API integration test suite,
When fetching an invalid document ID,
Then the HTTP response is exactly 404 and no body is generated.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Integration test coverage for missing entities
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Test pass rate for document isolation

epics.title: Remove End-User Telemetry Interface
epics.jtbd: When an end-user navigates the application, I want internal telemetry and tracking tabs to be hidden, so that the interface remains uncluttered and focused on epidemiological tasks.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduction in confusing end-user UI elements
epics.tocConstraintRef: Exposed Telemetry tab in main navigation
requirements: R1: The 'Телеметрия' tab must be completely removed from the end-user navigation UI.
R2: Any associated telemetry UI views must be disabled or restricted to isolated admin sections.

slices.title: Frontend Telemetry Removal
slices.jtbd: When updating the navigation for this epic, I want to remove the telemetry tab, so that users do not see internal metrics.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a regular user login,
When viewing the main navigation,
Then the 'Телеметрия' tab is entirely absent and inaccessible, while the UI remains WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.

slices.title: QA Telemetry Removal
slices.jtbd: When verifying the navigation for this epic, I want to ensure the telemetry tab cannot be accessed, so that the UI is clean.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the frontend application,
When attempting to navigate to the telemetry route or finding the tab,
Then the route does not exist and the tab is not rendered in the DOM.

epics.title: Disable Unsupported Mock Capabilities
epics.jtbd: When a researcher uses the application, I want unsupported UI features to be hidden or disabled, so that I am not misled by non-functional simulated actions.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Removal of test mechanics from production build
requirements: R1: The 'Симулировать остановленный бэкенд' and 'simulateNetworkError' checkboxes must be removed from the production UI.
R2: All mock simulation controls in the main catalog and upload forms must be restricted to isolated test environments only.

slices.title: Frontend Mock Control Removal
slices.jtbd: When cleaning the forms for this epic, I want to remove simulation toggles, so that the production UI is purely functional.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the catalog and upload forms,
When rendered in production,
Then no simulation checkboxes or network error toggles are visible, and the forms are WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.

slices.title: QA Mock Control Removal
slices.jtbd: When testing the forms for this epic, I want to ensure test mechanics are gone, so that user immersion is preserved.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the production frontend application,
When inspecting the catalog and upload interfaces,
Then the simulation controls are strictly absent from the DOM.

epics.title: Measurement: Epidemiological Analysis Speed
epics.jtbd: When the product is used in production, I want to measure the time it takes an epidemiologist to complete an analysis, so that we can prove the system delivers its core value of speed.
requirements: R1: Define the goal: Prove the system delivers epidemiological analysis speed.
R2: Define the questions: How long does a full analysis workflow take from start to finish? Are users completing the workflow?
R3: Implement non-intrusive backend measurement for analysis completion time to answer the defined questions.

slices.title: Backend Telemetry Measurement
slices.jtbd: When implementing the measurement for this epic, I want to record workflow completion times in the backend, so that we can answer the GQM questions.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an active epidemiological analysis,
When the workflow is completed,
Then the elapsed time is recorded in the backend metrics system without blocking the user flow.

epics.title: Initial Epidemiological Domain Content
epics.jtbd: When a client evaluates a fresh install, I want the system to be populated with real domain content, so that every step of the analytical dossier workflow is demonstrable.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Completeness of the demonstrable initial data
requirements: R1: The system must include realistic epidemiological strains and initial data sets.
R2: The content must be sufficient to exercise every link of the core analytical dossier workflow on a fresh install.

slices.title: Initial Content Generation
slices.jtbd: When generating seed data for this epic, I want to create realistic domain records, so that the product can be demonstrated immediately.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh deployment,
When the system starts,
Then the database is seeded with complete, realistic epidemiological records that satisfy all core workflow foreign keys.
